candidates.statement: Knot energies can help to model repulsive forces of fibres, whenever self-interaction of strands should be avoided.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{th:criticalpointchar}: (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2)] Observe for any $c > 0$, \[ \mathcal{E}^{\alpha,p}(c^{-1}\sol') = c^{\alpha p-2}\mathcal{E}^{\alpha,p}(\sol'), \] and \[ \tilde{\mathcal{E}}^{\alpha,p}(c^{-1}\sol') = c^{\alpha p-2}\tilde{\mathcal{E}}^{\alpha,p}(\sol'). \] Thus, we shall assume w.l.o.g. $\sol' = u$ (i.e. $c \equiv 1$) without changing anything about the criticality.
\begin{remark} We shall see that $\mathcal{R}_i(\solu,\cdot)$ are lower order terms which belong to $(L^1)^\ast$, see Proposition~\ref{pr:loterms}.

candidates.statement: Rather than providing a rigorous proof of the preceding statement by suitably decomposing the integration domain and carefully estimating based on techniques from~\cite{blatt-reiter-2008}, we illustrate the situation by providing a numerical experiment that supports the latter conjecture (and which we believe should be possible to be made rigorous with a careful, lengthy computation).
